quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Should you always drive slower than other cars?

options.text: No. Driving too slowly can block traffic.
Yes. It is good defensive driving.
Yes. It is always safer than driving faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: No. Driving too slowly can block traffic.
questions.explanation: Drive slowly in heavy traffic or bad weather. But if you block the normal flow of traffic by driving too slowly, you may get a ticket.

questions.question: You drive defensively when you:

options.text: Keep one car length between you and the car ahead.
Look only at the car in front of you.
Keep your eyes moving to spot hazards ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your eyes moving to spot hazards ahead.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means scanning ahead for dangers. Do not stare only at the road right in front of you. Look ahead and watch for vehicles around you.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly is not unsafe.
Driving too slowly on highways can be dangerous.
Speed does not affect safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too slowly on highways can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Slow driving can be dangerous. It frustrates drivers behind you, who may try unsafe passes. It is safest to drive with traffic flow, within the speed limit.

questions.question: Where should a 12-year-old sit in a car with airbags?

options.text: The front seat
The back seat
Any seat

questions.correctAnswerText: The back seat
questions.explanation: A child should not sit in the front passenger seat if the car has an airbag. An airbag can seriously hurt a child. State law requires all children under 14 to sit in the back seat and wear proper safety restraints while the car is moving.

questions.question: If you need to use your cell phone while driving, you should:

options.text: Keep phone calls short.
Stop in a safe parking area first.
Use a hands-free device and keep both hands on the wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop in a safe parking area first.
questions.explanation: Stop in a safe parking area before using your cell phone. Anything that takes your attention off driving is dangerous.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Jogging trail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign shows a crosswalk. When you see it, watch for people crossing and let them cross safely.

questions.question: A broken yellow line down the road means:

options.text: A construction zone is ahead.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Broken yellow lines separate traffic on two-lane roads. Any driver may pass when there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: You must go through the intersection at this speed.
The highest safe speed under good conditions is 55 mph.
You must not go slower than this speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest safe speed under good conditions is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the speed limit for that road. You can drive slower based on weather and road conditions, but you cannot drive faster than the posted limit.

questions.question: When should your wheels NOT point straight ahead?

options.text: When waiting to turn left at a traffic light.
When parked on a hill or slope.
When parked on a flat road with no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When parked on a hill or slope.
questions.explanation: Keep wheels straight when waiting to turn left. If hit from behind, this stops you from sliding into oncoming traffic. On a hill, turn wheels away from traffic so the car won't roll if brakes fail.

questions.question: A flashing red light at an intersection means:

options.text: The same as a yield sign.
The light is about to turn green.
The same as a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe. This is the same as a stop sign.

questions.question: Yellow lines separate:

options.text: Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of a two-way road. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. A broken yellow line means you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: To avoid losing traction on wet roads, you should:

options.text: Make abrupt turns.
Apply the brakes firmly.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down on wet roads to prevent skidding. Keep your tires in good condition. If you lose control, release the gas and brakes, stay calm, and let the car slow down naturally.

questions.question: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means that vehicles:

options.text: Driving in both directions may pass.
Next to the broken line may pass.
Next to the solid line may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Next to the broken line may pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. If you have a broken yellow line next to you, you can pass.

questions.question: If your vehicle begins to skid, you should:

options.text: Ease up on the gas pedal.
Brake as hard as possible.
Turn off the ignition.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ease up on the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, release the gas or brake pedal. Steer in the direction the back of your car is sliding to regain control.

questions.question: Check your rearview mirrors:

options.text: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot.
Only when you are slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirrors frequently while driving. This helps you know where other vehicles are near you.

questions.question: If a vehicle ahead is approaching at night with high beam headlights on:

options.text: Quickly flash your headlights one time.
Do not dim your high beam headlights.
Look in the direction of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Quickly flash your headlights one time.
questions.explanation: Flash your headlights once to signal the other driver to dim their lights. If they do not, look toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded. Do not use your high beams in response.

questions.question: If a traffic signal is green and a police officer signals you to stop, you should:

options.text: Obey the officer.
Obey the traffic signal.
Do what the vehicle in front of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Obey the officer.
questions.explanation: Always obey a police officer's directions, even if they go against traffic signals, signs, or road markings.

questions.question: When preparing to turn left from a two-way street, you should drive:

options.text: Near the right-hand side of the road.
Near the centerline.
On the left of the centerline.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the centerline.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a two-way street, stay in the lane closest to the center. Turn just before your car reaches the intersection center. Do not cut the corner.

questions.question: If you see a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane:

options.text: The pedestrian must yield the right-of-way.
You must yield the right-of-way.
Honk your horn to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A guide dog or white cane means the person is blind or partially blind. You must yield the right-of-way to this person.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Flagger ahead.
Turn left at the intersection.
Last turn before a toll road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flagger ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs and cones mark work zones. Stay alert when you see orange signs. This sign warns you that a flagger is ahead. Obey all flagger directions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School zone or school crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: School zone or school crossing.
questions.explanation: A yellow or yellow-green five-sided sign warns drivers about a school zone or school crossing.

questions.question: A large truck ahead is turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction. What may the truck do?

options.text: Complete its turn using either of the two lanes.
Swing wide to complete the right turn.
Stay in the right lane at all times while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Swing wide to complete the right turn.
questions.explanation: When turning, the rear wheels follow a shorter path than the front wheels. Long trucks need more space, so they often swing wide to complete a right turn.

questions.question: When must you always stop before crossing railroad tracks?

options.text: When there is no room on the other side to completely cross the tracks.
When the crossing is in a city with frequent train traffic.
When you are carrying two or more young children.

questions.correctAnswerText: When there is no room on the other side to completely cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: A train can come on any track at any time. Never stop your vehicle on the tracks. Cross completely before you stop.

questions.question: On roadways, bicycles are considered:

options.text: Hazards.
Vehicles.
Dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles on roadways. Cyclists and drivers must follow the same traffic rules.

questions.question: What does this sign tell you?

options.text: No turns are allowed on this road.
The road narrows ahead.
There are curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There are curves ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to road conditions ahead. This sign warns you about a winding road.
